Volume 16 assessment — specialization and original research

Turn a question into an auditable argument, and distinguish a rehearsed research skill from an original contribution accepted by qualified readers.

This package contains a prerequisite diagnostic, two distinct written forms, an open-resource research rehearsal, oral transfer and delayed retention. Every supplied study, bank record and numerical model is an original synthetic teaching case. A score measures performance on this material. Actual scholarship also requires a learner-generated contribution, warranted access to evidence, transparent limitations and substantive external evaluation. Keep the first attempt, feedback, corrections and version history.

Prerequisite diagnostic

Before studying this volume, allow a proposed 75 minutes, using paper and a basic calculator without notes or code. Eight tasks carry 5 points each. Readiness requires 34/40 and correction of every critical identification, unit, feasibility or integrity error. The tasks diagnose earlier quantitative and empirical reasoning; definitions needed here are supplied. Use the routes in the answers for remediation and explain a changed example without the key before returning. Timing and thresholds are instructional choices, not empirically calibrated standards.

  1. Choose a growth estimand. Two banks have opening loan stocks (50,80), and closing stocks (55,72), in the same million-currency units. Compute each growth rate, the equal-bank mean, and aggregate stock growth. Show the weighting identity. Does any result measure new loan originations?
  2. Supply the missing counterfactual. An exposed group has mean outcome (before,after) (20,18); a comparison group has (30,33). Define D as exposed change minus comparison change. Compute D. Give two complete counterfactual mean stories consistent with these observations: one satisfying parallel untreated changes and one with zero intervention effect. Assume no anticipation and an unaffected comparison group. Are equal initial levels required?
  3. Condition correctly. The probabilities (high state, positive given high, positive given low) are (1/4,3/4,1/4). Compute the probability of a positive signal and the posterior high-state probability after it. Explain what changes if only selected positive records enter the dataset.
  4. Prove a model optimum. A quasilinear consumer has gross benefit B(q)=9q−q²/2, and a competitive producer has cost C(q)=q+q²/2, q≥0. Assume sufficient numeraire and no externalities. Derive equilibrium quantity and price, prove global surplus maximization, and calculate the surplus lost if quantity is restricted to 3.
  5. Interpret an interval. In a stipulated normal location model with known standard error, (estimate, standard error, rounded two-sided critical value) are (0.4,0.5,1.96). Using that critical value, compute the approximate 95% interval. Does failure to reject a zero effect prove zero? Is a positive effect of 1 excluded?
  6. Bound incomplete measurement. Inputs (observed share, observed mean, lower outcome bound, upper outcome bound) are (3/4,4,0,8) for a fixed population. Outcomes are continuous and every outcome, observed or not, lies within those bounds. Give the sharp bounds for the full population mean and show endpoint and interior attainability. Why is reporting 4 alone insufficient?
  7. Distinguish rerunning from correctness. A script reports stock growth as (end−start)/end. With (start,end)=(100,120), its saved output exactly matches a fresh run. The intended definition is change divided by opening stock. Compute both numbers and write a correction instruction that preserves the ability to reconstruct the original release.
  8. Make a feasible evidence claim. An analyst proposes: “Our selected six banks prove that funding access raises national lending.” Only before/after bank stock totals are supplied; no assignment or counterfactual evidence exists. The analyst has (capacity, source/data checks, analysis, writing, review) hours (120,40,30,30,30). Calculate feasibility, write a defensible one-sentence claim, and propose an exact budget repair that preserves source checks and review.
Complete answers and additive scoring

  1. Individual growth rates are (55−50)/50=1/10 and (72−80)/80=−1/10. Their equal-bank mean is zero, whereas total stock falls from 130 to 127. (1/10,-1/10,0,-3/130) lists these four results. Aggregate growth uses opening-stock weights: (50/130)(1/10)+(80/130)(−1/10)=−3/130. Equal-bank growth answers a different question. Stocks combine new lending, repayments, defaults, sales and other adjustments; they do not identify gross originations. Specify the population, weighting and stock definition before using either result.

    Rubric (5 points). Individual rates 1; equal mean 1; aggregate 1; weighting identity 1; stock/origination distinction 1. Review data construction and stock and flow accounts.

  2. D=(18−20)−(33−30)=−5. Let m be the exposed group’s after-period mean without intervention. Its effect is τ=18−m; differential untreated change is b=(m−20)−3=m−23, hence D=τ+b. Parallel changes set m=23, giving (τ,b)=(−5,0). Zero effect sets m=18, giving (0,−5). Thus (-5,23,-5,0,18,0,-5) records D and the two triples (m,τ,b). Both reproduce all four observed means. The initial level gap does not contradict parallel changes, and neither observed change alone establishes the restriction on m. These are mean stories; they do not impose equal individual effects.

    Rubric (5 points). Observed D 1; identity 1; first world 1; second world 1; assumption versus levels 1. Review difference-in-differences.

  3. The joint high-and-positive probability is 3/16; the low-and-positive probability is also 3/16. The signal probability and posterior are therefore (3/8,1/2). The posterior follows from exhaustive states and the stated likelihoods for the signal actually observed. Selection into a record can alter the relevant conditional probabilities. If retention differs by state even after conditioning on the signal, the supplied signal likelihoods are insufficient for the posterior among retained records; one needs retention probabilities as well.

    Rubric (5 points). Two joint probabilities 2; denominator 1; posterior 1; selection condition 1. Review conditional probability.

  4. Marginal benefit is 9−q and marginal cost is 1+q. Clearing yields q=4 and p=5. Total surplus is S(q)=8q−q²=16−(q−4)², so its global maximum on q≥0 is 16, uniquely at 4. At q=3 it is 15, a loss of 1. The checked results are (4,5,16,15,1). This calculation is conditional on the supplied preferences, technology, competition and absence of other effects. The price transfers numeraire between the two agents and is not a separate social resource loss.

    Rubric (5 points). Marginal equations 1; equilibrium 1; global proof 1; restricted surplus/loss 1; maintained conditions and transfer interpretation 1. Review competitive equilibrium and concavity.

  5. The margin is 1.96×0.5=0.98, giving (-0.58,1.38). Zero is inside, so the corresponding two-sided test does not reject it. One is also inside and is not excluded by this interval. Failure to reject is compatible with a range of substantively different effects; it is not proof of zero. In repeated draws under the stipulated normal model, intervals made this way have approximately 95% coverage because the quantile was rounded. This is not a 95% posterior probability that the fixed parameter lies inside the realized interval, nor evidence that the normal model holds in an application.

    Rubric (5 points). Margin 1; endpoints 1; zero-test interpretation 1; effect of 1 interpretation 1; sampling/conditional coverage 1. Review estimation and intervals.

  6. Writing μmiss for the missing mean gives μ=(3/4)4+(1/4)μmiss=3+μmiss/4. The sharp bounds are (3,5). Set every missing outcome to 0 or 8 to reach the endpoints. For any desired μ in [3,5], setting each missing outcome to 4(μ−3) realizes it and remains within [0,8]. The observations do not determine μmiss; reporting the observed mean as the population mean adds a missingness or equal-mean restriction. The interval concerns the finite population, not sampling uncertainty.

    Rubric (5 points). Population identity 1; endpoints 2; sharpness including interior 1; selection/uncertainty distinction 1. Review selection and missing data.

  7. The recorded code produces 20/120=1/6; the intended growth is 20/100=1/5. Thus (1/6,1/5). A suitable instruction is: “Retain the original input, code and output as version 0. Make a separately identified corrected version using opening stock as denominator, add a hand calculation and zero-opening-stock rejection, rerun all dependent tables and replace each affected claim. Record the changed definition and the numerical discrepancy.” Matching saved output establishes a narrow computational agreement, not validity of the formula, source data or causal claim.

    Rubric (5 points). Faithful output 1; intended output 1; version preservation 1; dependent correction/test 1; reproduction/correctness distinction 1. Review reproducibility.

  8. The schedule totals 130 hours and exceeds capacity by 10: (130,10,40,20,30,30) gives total, shortfall and one repaired allocation. Narrow the analysis to a descriptive six-bank stock reconciliation requiring 20 hours, retain 40 for source/data checks, 30 for writing and 30 for review, and confirm that this smaller analysis is feasible before committing. A defensible claim is: “The supplied records describe changes in outstanding lending for six selected banks; they do not identify a funding-access effect or a national response.” The repair changes scope explicitly; it does not pretend the original causal project became valid by shortening its schedule. Access failure or unusable records triggers reconsideration rather than fabrication.

    Rubric (5 points). Total/shortfall 1; exact feasible allocation 1; explicit reduced scope 1; descriptive claim 1; causal/population limits 1. Review policy synthesis and empirical project design.

Administration and advancement

Form A constructs a research argument from supplied notes and records. Form B audits and repairs a different argument. Each has twenty 5-point tasks across five 20-point domains, totaling 100. For each form allow a proposed 240 minutes, closed book, with paper and a basic nonprogrammable calculator; no code or internet. Required constants and case materials are supplied. Answer prompts before opening their solutions. The forms are substantively different but have not been statistically equated or timed with learners.

Essential domains in both written forms and the project
DomainChapter routesWhat the learner must demonstrate
Question, literature and judgment1, 2, 4A feasible contribution, traceable evidence map and constructive referee reasoning
Reproduction, data and ethics3, 7Versions, measurement, linkage, missingness and warranted access/release
Model, identification and design5, 6, 8An estimand, global model solution, counterfactual restrictions and prospective design
Robustness and writing9, 10Uncertainty, sensitivity, transport conditions and claims that match evidence
Defense and portfolio11, 12Unfamiliar questions, documented revision and credible continuation of real research

For written-form advancement require at least 85/100 overall, at least 15/20 in every domain, repair of all critical errors and a successful unseen transfer explanation. Critical errors include changing the population or units without disclosure, treating an unidentified association as causal, releasing data without warranted authority, hiding a consequential correction, or inventing source inspection or external approval. Additive rubrics award each stated point once; equivalent valid derivations earn credit. After targeted remediation and a study interval, administer the other form. Do not count reading a solution as an independent successful attempt.

The project is open resource and separately scored. The complete teaching dossier permits actual reconstruction, correction, model checks, writing and defense practice. Record tools and assistance, rerun the downloadable standard-library Python materials, and compare an independently constructed calculation with the instructor output. The project’s five-domain score cannot certify novelty or real research competence. The continuation requirements demand an actual question, full source reading, authorized data access where relevant, learner-generated paper and qualified independent evaluation. The separate research portfolio capstone is a distinct production item; its status is displayed on the assessment index.

Volume 16 — Form A: construct a defensible research argument

Conditions. Proposed 240-minute closed-book assessment; basic calculator permitted, no code, internet or external papers required. All needed evidence is supplied below. Twenty questions carry five points each, organized in five 20-point domains. Timing and equivalence with Form B are uncalibrated teaching proposals. This form emphasizes construction; Form B uses different material for audit and repair.

Advancement rule. At least85/100 overall and15/20 in every domain, followed by correction of every critical error and a distinct unseen transfer task. A high total cannot compensate for fabricated evidence, unsupported causal or novelty claims, unauthorized release, or a fundamental target/unit error. These are authored assessment rules, not institutional certification. Passing this rehearsal does not establish an original research contribution or external human approval.

Write concise complete artifacts rather than lists of section names. All banks, studies, permissions and numbers are fictional. Use exact fractions or sensible stated rounding. For later writing tasks, a clearly carried-forward arithmetic slip may earn the relevant writing/logic marks; do not award correctness of a wrong numeric result twice. Unsupported causal language or silent changes in target are separate substantive errors. The rubric awards five independent one-point criteria per question; equivalent defensible answers earn those points.

Supplied research dossier

Researcher and scope. You know bank accounting and reproducible data construction and have basic causal-inference training. You have60 hours over ten weeks for an initial research scoping stage. Only the synthetic materials here are immediately usable. No real borrower-linked access, field intervention, ethics determination or novelty review has occurred. A later real paper must have its own authorization, source inspection and qualified evaluation.

Cedar note: a randomized documentation-assistance offer

This complete fictional short note asks whether offering assistance with working-capital loan documentation changes an eligible bank's ninety-day net advances. Six banks are fixed before assignment; three are selected uniformly for the offer. Terms and outcome construction are common, all outcomes are observed, and the teaching design assumes no cross-bank interference. Observed net advances, in millions, are(3,4,5) for offered banks and(1,2,3) for controls. The note reports offered mean4 minus control mean2, a realized contrast of2. Under the lottery, the mean-difference estimator is unbiased for the equal-bank roster average offer effect. One realized contrast need not equal that effect. The note contains no borrower identifiers, no lender substitution data, no receipt-effect design and no national extrapolation. Its supported contribution is a transparent small design demonstration, not actual empirical evidence or proof of a mechanism.

Maple note: a borrower replacement account

This complete fictional short note observes three borrowers selected because their original lender reduced credit. Changes at that lender are(-3,-2,-1) million; changes at other lenders are(2,2,1). There is no missing credit source within these invented borrower records. Summing across lenders yields borrower changes(−1,0,0): mean−1/3, compared with original-lender mean−2. The note correctly describes partial replacement in this selected sample. No assistance offer was randomly assigned, no untreated comparison is supplied and no time-varying demand restriction is justified. The author's concluding sentence is: “Replacement proves documentation assistance has no effect on borrowers.” That sentence is an unsupported inference beyond the supplied accounting.

Pine candidate. A fictional search result contains only this abstract: “We study annual funding composition and loan growth in a national panel.” Its body, data dictionary, identification argument and bibliography have not been inspected. Treat it as a candidate for reading, not corroborating evidence. Cedar, Maple and Pine are invented reading materials, not publications to cite as real studies.

Complete synthetic transaction extract, release r1; rows with the same event ID are reports of the same event
Raw rowEvent IDBank codeKindAmountUnit
r01e01K7advance1200thousand
r02e02K7repayment300thousand
r03e03M4advance0.8million
r04e03M4advance800thousand

Dictionary and provenance. K7 maps to bankA, M4 toB, R2 toC; the mapping is one-to-one and fixed. All events occur inside the same ninety-day window and currency. The source explicitly confirms that e03's two reports describe one event with equivalent amounts, not two loans. Event IDs are globally unique after removing that duplicate. A zero is observed, not a missing value; there are no missing amounts here. Net advances mean advances minus principal repayments. This ledger is a separate measurement fixture, not the Cedar outcome file.

Benchmark and later revision. An old benchmark converts every raw row to millions, sums advances, subtracts repayments and reports2.4 million. It does not remove duplicate event IDs. A later authoritative exercise revision r2 changes only e02 from300 to350 thousand; preserve r1. This is a stipulated synthetic correction, not a new observation from a real bank.

Hypothetical access brief. For a future real-data analogue, the custodian permits named researchers to analyze raw transactions only in a controlled environment. A bank-level aggregate may leave only after the custodian's disclosure review; transaction IDs and the linkage key may not be exported. Separate approval for the proposed research purpose has not yet been resolved. These are this exercise's stipulated conditions, not universal law. All displayed teaching data remain wholly invented.

Model fixture. In a separate one-period competitive credit model, borrower benefit is B(Q)=12Q−Q²/2, Q≥0. Sector cost is C(q)=3q+(q−D)+², q≥0,D≥0, with u+=max(u,0). Both take price R≥0 as given; the borrower maximizes B(Q)−RQ, the sector maximizes Rq−C(q), and Q=q clears. Q,q,D are loan units; R is numeraire per loan unit, not a percentage interest rate. D is exogenous internal financing capacity. The primitive tuple(a,b,c,γ) is(12,1,3,2), where marginal benefit is a−bQ and marginal cost is c+γ(q−D)+. There is no default, aggregate feedback or cost of acquiring D in this fixture.

Power fixture. For a proposed future single-primary-outcome trial, assume independent bank outcomes with a constant offer effectδ=1 million and known normal standard deviationσ=2 million. Equal allocation gives n per arm and standard error s=σ√(2/n). Use a two-sided level0.05 normal test with supplied critical value c=1.959964. Its power is Φ(δ/s−c)+Φ(−δ/s−c). Supplied values: Φ(0.540036)=0.705414 and Φ(−4.459964)=0.000004; exact-expression powers at n=62 and63 round to0.795008 and0.801302. Power is increasing in positive integer n for this positive effect. Only100 banks are currently feasible; (σ,δ,c)=(2,1,1.959964). These are hypothetical planning assumptions, not estimated dispersions or exact power of an estimated-variance real analysis.

Uncertainty and transport fixtures. A separate observational contrast has estimate2 million and known normal standard error0.5; θ=τ+b, with possible upward bias0≤b≤1.2. Use z=1.96 for an approximately95% central normal interval. The tuple(estimate,standard error,bias budget,z) is(2,0.5,1.2,1.96). This is not a standard error estimated from Cedar's six observations. Separately, known source conditional effects for high/low external dependence are(3,1) million, source shares(3/5,2/5), and destination shares(1/5,4/5). These are population arithmetic inputs. A hypothetical declared three-estimator display for one common ITT target reports unadjusted2.0, fixed pre-period adjustment1.6 and fitted common-slope adjustment1.8 million, all using the same observations. The fitted adjustment has additional modeling requirements. These estimates are stipulated; they are not generated by the transaction ledger.

Portfolio fixture. A later100-hour stage currently allocates40 hours to data/provenance work,15 to a theory extension,20 to a short paper,15 to external-review responses and10 reserve. A newly required20-hour purpose/access review would precede dependent real-data work. The data, paper and response allowances must be retained. No reviewer has agreed, no real computation has been completed and no real contribution has been accepted.

I. Question, literature and judgment —20 points

Bounded chapter coverage: C01, C02, C04.

  1. Construct a feasible initial research question and a60-hour scope contract using the researcher brief. Give an economic reason to care, the immediate deliverable, one later extension and a concrete stop/pivot rule. (5 points)
  2. Construct a three-row evidence map for Cedar, Maple and Pine: question/unit, method, supported result and unresolved limitation. State why Cedar and Maple do not provide contradictory estimates of one effect. (5 points)
  3. Write a bounded next-reading protocol for a real literature search on bank assistance and borrower replacement. Give two concept-based search combinations, a citation-chain step, required extraction fields and a defensible rule for the novelty statement. Do not invent a publication or completed search. (5 points)
  4. Write a short referee report on Maple: summarize its contribution, identify the major claim error with an alternative explanation, give an achievable revision and distinguish one optional extension from a required repair. (5 points)

II. Reproduction, data and ethics —20 points

Bounded chapter coverage: C03, C07.

  1. Construct the release-r1 analysis ledger in millions: one row per unique event, its signed net-flow contribution, bank totals and the total. Explain the duplicate decision and the observed-zero treatment. (5 points)
  2. Write a faithful reproduction and discrepancy report for the old benchmark, then give corrected deduplicated totals for r1 and r2. Distinguish reproduced computation, repaired measurement and what the correction cannot establish. (5 points)
  3. Specify an executable-in-principle dataset construction contract for r2: grain/key, mapping cardinality, units/signs, duplicate conflict rule, version/output links and validation checks. Include the final three bank net flows. (5 points)

Form B — Audit and repair a refinancing research packet

Administration. Proposed 240 minutes, closed book, no code or internet; a basic calculator is permitted. All needed evidence and normal-distribution constants are supplied. Twenty prompts carry 5 points each: five domains of 20, total 100. Show reasoning and write the requested replacement text. These timing and equivalence proposals are uncalibrated. Supplied packet: all institutions, notes, data and reviews below are fictional

A research team studies a refinancing-information invitation offered to eight banks. Four banks were selected uniformly from the eight for invitation; the realized allocation is T1–T4. Invitation Z is assigned; attendance R is a subsequent bank choice. The primary descriptive outcome Y is 1 if the bank's six-month loan balance is at least its baseline balance and 0 otherwise. The intended causal target is the equal-bank average effect of invitation on Y for this fixed eight-bank roster, under consistency and no interference. Random assignment supports an unbiased full-roster difference in means over assignments when outcomes are observed; it does not reveal each bank's counterfactual or remove missingness. Attendance effects need additional assumptions. No observed bank outcome establishes borrower investment or total economy-wide credit.

Loan balances are in millions of one common currency at constant units; the baseline perimeter is fixed. There are no hidden mergers or unit conversions. “Unknown” means no verified balance; it is not zero. The delivery table is the complete release-2 input. Event e2 appears twice because it was transmitted twice: exact duplicate event IDs must be retained once. Distinct IDs would be distinct records; a conflicting duplicate would need a source query, not automatic averaging. Attendance is observed for every bank.

Note M, complete short submission (fictional, version 2). “Invitation, attendance and lending preservation.” Question: does attending refinancing information protect lending? Method: use the above eight-bank experiment but compare the two invited attendees with the three observed controls. Both attendees maintain lending, while one control does. The estimated gap is 2/3. Interpretation: attendance causes lending preservation, because the invitation was randomized. T4 and C4 are omitted because they did not report a final balance. Our receipt comparison is new because we use the term ‘refinancing resilience’; no comparison with a prior receipt study is supplied. We recommend a national rollout. Limitation: eight banks give limited precision. Model card. A bank chooses q in [0,K] to maximize (a−c)q−q²/2. Here q and K are normalized loan units, a−c has the corresponding marginal-value units, K≥0 and a,c≥0. The upper bound is a financing capacity, not a demand estimate. All primitives are fixed within each comparison except K. Consider a−c=6 with K rising from 3 to 5, and separately a−c=2 with the same capacity change. The quadratic coefficient is normalized to one. This is an original partial-equilibrium model with no outside lender or default, not a fitted explanation of the eight banks.

Prospective design card. A separate future study would randomize independent banks equally between invitation and control, with a continuous six-month net-lending outcome. For planning only, each outcome is independent normal with known common σ=0.4 million, an additive invitation effect δ=0.2 million and n banks per arm. Thus the difference in sample means is normal with mean δ and variance 2σ²/n. Reject a zero-effect null when |difference/SE|>1.96, a conventional approximately 5% two-sided test. Compare n values (32,64); available capacity is 128 banks. Use Φ(0.04)=0.51595344, Φ(−3.96)=0.00003747, Φ(0.86842712)=0.80741972 and Φ(−4.78842712)=0.00000084. Form B — Complete answers and additive scoring

Open all Form B solutions and rubrics

Let u=Y(T4) and v=Y(C4), each in {0,1}. The full-roster observed-assignment contrast would be (2+u)/4−(1+v)/4=(1+u−v)/4. Invited mean lies in [1/2,3/4], control mean in [1/4,1/2], and difference in (0,1/2). Assignments (u,v)=(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1) yield (1/4,0,1/2,1/4). Thus endpoints are attainable and the exact feasible grid is {0,1/4,1/2}; the enclosing interval is a convenient bound. These are missing-outcome possibilities for the realized group contrast, not sampling uncertainty or potential-outcome counterfactual information. B09

Index the receiving bank A and nonreceiving bank B. A zero-effect world sets (Y_A(0),Y_A(1))=(1,1) and (Y_B(0),Y_B(1))=(0,0): both individual effects and the average are zero. A unit-effect world sets both pairs to (0,1): both effects and the average are one. The observed received outcome for A is 1 and the unreceived outcome for B is 0 in both worlds. The two average effects are (0,1), proving that this receipt association alone cannot identify the receipt effect. Random invitation can identify an invitation estimand under its assumptions and complete observation; it does not randomize attendance, supply an exclusion restriction or monotonicity, reveal missing Y, or establish economy-wide effects. Any receipt analysis must defend its own assumptions and target.

Additive 5-point rubric: Complete zero-effect schedule (1); Complete unit-effect schedule (1); Verifies identical observed pairs (1); Computes both average effects and identification implication (1); Invitation/receipt and missingness distinction (1).

B10

The objective has derivative a−c−q and second derivative −1, so it is strictly concave. For a−c≤0 it is nonincreasing on the feasible set and q*=0. For a−c>0 it increases up to a−c and decreases afterward; restricting to [0,K] gives q*=min{max(a−c,0),K}, including K=0 and equality boundaries. Strict concavity gives a unique choice. With a−c=6, capacities 3 and 5 imply q=(3,5), a gain 2; with a−c=2 they imply q=(2,2), gain 0. The levels/gains are (3,5,2,2,2,0). With fixed a,c, increasing K cannot reduce this bank’s lending, and a slack cap has zero marginal effect. A fall after a capacity increase challenges the maintained model or fixed-primitives premise, but does not isolate which failed. This partial-equilibrium choice says nothing by itself about substitution at other lenders.

Additive 5-point rubric: Correct concavity/derivative argument (1); Global clipped solution with boundaries (1); Correct constrained numerical case (1); Correct slack numerical case (1); Conditional falsifiable implication and scope limitation (1).

B11

Write D̂/SE=Z+δ/SE with Z standard normal and SE=σ√(2/n). Rejection occurs when Z>1.96−δ/SE or Z<−1.96−δ/SE; disjoint tails give power Φ(δ/SE−1.96)+Φ(−δ/SE−1.96). At n=32, SE=0.10 and δ/SE=2, so power=0.51595344+0.00003747≈0.51599091. At n=64, SE=√(1/200)≈0.07071068, shift≈2.82842712 and power=0.80741972+0.00000084≈0.80742056. The two rounded powers are (0.51599091,0.80742056). Of these two candidates, 64 per arm meets 80% and uses exactly 128 banks. This is not a claim about the smallest feasible integer n. Known normal variance, independence, implemented invitation effect and full observation are planning assumptions; estimated-variance testing, attrition, clustering or weaker take-up can change actual power.

Additive 5-point rubric: Derives SE (1); Derives both tails (1); Correct n32 computation (1); Correct n64 computation and candidate/capacity decision (1); States planning assumptions and implementation limits (1).

For fixed b, θ=δ−b and its normal interval is [D̂−1.96s−b,D̂+1.96s−b]. Union over b∈[−B,B] gives [D̂−1.96s−B,D̂+1.96s+B]. With D̂=0.30,s=0.10,B=0.20 the endpoints are (-12/125,87/125), or [−0.096,0.696]. For the true fixed b in the maintained set, the event |D̂−δ|≤1.96s implies θ belongs to its own interval and hence to the union; therefore coverage is at least 2Φ(1.96)−1, approximately 95%. This is not a posterior probability for θ, and the guarantee is conditional on the bias bound and normal law. The zero-endpoint radius is B*=0.30−0.196=13/125=0.104; strict positivity requires B<B*. These are future deliverables, not achievements supplied by this exam. A real original-paper requirement cannot be satisfied by renaming the synthetic example.

Research project — does funding support add credit or move it?

Population, timing, units and release history

Six fictional origin banks A–F each define a cohort of100 original borrowers before the offer. The cohorts are disjoint, fixed and equally sized; borrowers remain in their original cohort even if they change lender. The three pairs are P1=(A,B), P2=(C,D), P3=(E,F). Within each pair exactly one origin bank receives an offer; the three fair lotteries are independent. The displayed assignment offers A,C,E. This is a stipulated design, not evidence that a real lottery occurred. Causal interpretation additionally requires no anticipation, consistent implementation and no spillovers between cohorts. Other lenders' response within an offered cohort is part of that cohort's total-credit outcome; interference across cohorts would violate the setup.

Date0 is immediately before assignment; date1 is ninety days afterward. “Own” is cohort credit at its origin bank; “other” is that same cohort's credit across all other lenders. Both are stocks, measured in one currency on the same dates. Their sum is total cohort credit, not new originations, spending or welfare. Every raw value is an integer number of thousands; divide by1000to report millions. Each cohort receives equal weight. Because all cohorts contain100borrowers, equal-cohort and equal-borrower weighting differ only in the reporting scale here; that simplification would fail with unequal sizes.

Supplied research note A — “Funding offers and borrower credit,” first release

Identity and question. This original synthetic note asks whether a temporary funding offer expands total credit to the origin banks' original borrowers. It uses the complete version0ledger above. It is a short argument supplied for criticism, not a bibliographic claim that a real paper exists.

Design and estimator. Define ΔY as date1minus date0total cohort credit. In each pair subtract the non-offered cohort's change from the offered cohort's change, and average the three differences. The paired lottery motivates this statistic as an estimator of the equal-cohort average assignment effect, subject to no interference and the measurement contract. Own-bank changes are(10,2,14,2,18,2). Version0total changes are(16,2,4,2,4,2), so pair contrasts are(14,2,2)and their mean is6million. Own-bank contrasts are(8,12,16), averaging12; other-lender contrasts are(6,−10,−14), averaging−6. Components reconcile to6.

Argument offered by the note. “All three total-credit contrasts are positive, so the offer conclusively creates additional borrower credit. The12million own-bank gain is partly offset elsewhere, leaving6million additional credit per offered cohort. The pair lottery removes demand concerns. The same funding program should therefore increase national credit and welfare.” These sentences intentionally invite substantive review. The first confuses signs with uncertainty; the last extends the target without a transport or welfare argument. Even a credible lottery would identify an assignment effect, not uniquely a liquidity mechanism.

What is actually supplied. The full registry, component ledger, assignment rule and result calculation are available. No outcomes under the other assignments, observation sampling model, borrower welfare data, national target weights or actual institutional access records are supplied. A randomization test of the sharp null is possible from these observed outcomes under the stated design; a generic confidence claim about the average effect needs more argument. Version1restates the A entry but leaves the original release intact for faithful reproduction.

Supplied research note B — “A funding-cost model with borrower substitution”

Question and primitives. This separate original theoretical note asks how cheaper funding can raise lending at the supported bank while generating a smaller borrower-credit gain. For type i, a bank chooses x≥0to maximize Jᵢ(x)=(a−r)x−hᵢx²/2subject to x≤Kᵢ. x is an incremental loan-stock quantity in millions; a and r are benefit and effective funding-cost coefficients per unit in the model's objective, not measured annual interest rates. hᵢ>0is curvature. A subsidy s reduces cost from r₀to r₀−s, with0≤s≤r₀. The three types correspond to pairs, one offered bank of each type. Assume a=r₀=10, so the baseline optimum is zero. Methods available for the dossier

Faithful reconstruction asks whether the supplied version0inputs produce Note A's number. Correction asks what version1changes. They are different outputs. The National Academies' scoped discussion distinguishes computational reproduction using the same inputs from replication using new data; this project uses the former vocabulary without claiming universal terminology.[1] The retained AEA documentation benchmark supports recording provenance, transformations and output mappings; it supplies no permission to release a future restricted dataset.[2]

A literature map should separate related questions, units, designs, mechanisms and unresolved comparisons. The accepted scoped readings of Khwaja–Mian's author draft and Schnabl's author draft provide method context for linked borrowers, bank liquidity shocks and separating bank exposure from borrower demand.[3][4] No estimate or full-paper replication from either is imported. Read their stated scope in Chapter2before making a claim about those works; the map below is purposely bounded.

For referee judgment, reconstruct the best supported argument, identify consequences for the principal claim, and distinguish necessary repair from an optional extension. Every numerical proof needed for this original dossier is supplied in the instructor artifacts.

Complete instructor artifacts, proofs and answers

1. Evidence map and two complete referee reports

Question statement: Does an offer to an origin bank increase ninety-day total credit to its pre-offer borrower cohort, or mainly redistribute that cohort's borrowing across lenders? The primary finite-roster estimand is the mean assignment effect on total cohort credit over all six cohorts. The origin-bank component is a secondary outcome. The observed estimator compares offered versus non-offered changes within pairs; it is not a realized individual treatment effect. Mechanism, national scale and welfare are further questions.

3. Global model, exact inference and identification limits

Global optimum proof. J is continuous on compact[0,K], so a maximizer exists. For h>0, J″=−h<0, so it is unique whenever the interval contains more than one point; when K=0the only feasible choice is0. Let q=(a−r)/h. Completing the square gives J(x)=−h(x−q)²/2+(a−r)²/(2h). Maximizing J therefore minimizes distance to qover[0,K], yielding x*=max(0,min(K,q)). If a−r≤0, choose0; if0<a−r<hK, choose(a−r)/h; if a−r≥hK, chooseK. Equality at either boundary gives the same unique value. This proves global optimality, including corners, rather than merely reporting a first-order condition.

With a=r₀, subsidy s produces xᵢ(s)=min(Kᵢ,s/hᵢ). Capacity starts binding at hK=(5,14/3,9/2). Below its threshold a type's derivative is1/h; above it the derivative is0, with a kink at the threshold. Borrower gain is(1−λ)x, so it is weakly increasing in s only if λ≤1is maintained. With λ>1it can fall as the supported bank expands. The subsidy spending identity is sΣxᵢ(s), which includes transfers to modeled lending rather than net additional borrower credit. It is a budget account, not a social welfare calculation.

Design expectation. In a pair with cohorts i,j, let Yᵢ(z)be the date1total under own offer status zand let Bᵢbe the fixed baseline. When iis offered the pair statistic is[Yᵢ(1)−Bᵢ]−[Yⱼ(0)−Bⱼ]; when jis offered it is[Yⱼ(1)−Bⱼ]−[Yᵢ(0)−Bᵢ]. Averaging these equally likely cases cancels baseline terms and gives{[Yᵢ(1)−Yᵢ(0)]+[Yⱼ(1)−Yⱼ(0)]}/2. Averaging the three pairs gives the equal-cohort six-unit mean assignment effect. The same argument applies to each component. It assumes outcomes do not depend on other cohorts' assignments; no arithmetic can establish that assumption. The observed estimate need not equal the estimand in this one realization.

Exact sharp-null test. Under Yᵢ(1)=Yᵢ(0)for every cohort, observed changes are fixed. Flipping which cohort is offered flips a pair difference's sign. The eight independent sign patterns are equally likely; use the absolute mean as the prespecified two-sided statistic. Version0reference means are (-6,-14/3,-14/3,-10/3,10/3,14/3,14/3,6). Version1reference means are (-2,-2/3,-2/3,2/3,-2/3,2/3,2/3,2). Both have two values at least as extreme as their observed mean, so(tail,count,p)=(2,8,1/4). Neither rejects at5%. The smallest attainable two-sided p-value for these nonzero symmetric endpoint cases is1/4, so this tiny design cannot deliver5%rejection with this statistic even for an extreme observed sign pattern.

For size, order the eight absolute reference values from greatest to least and assign each value its inclusive upper-tail probability. Ties receive the entire tied upper tail. At most an αfraction of assignments can have a tail probability at mostα; uniform assignment therefore gives Pr(p≤α)≤α. This finite proof preserves the actual paired lottery. It is a sharp-null test: a zero average with offsetting individual effects does not fix all missing counterfactuals, so the sign-flip list is not automatically a weak-average-null distribution. Nonrejection does not establish zero.

A concrete identification distinction. The observed corrected table is compatible with a constant total effect2for every cohort: set every untreated total change to2and every treated total change to4. It is also compatible with zero effects for every cohort, with fixed changes4for A,C,E and2for B,D,F. Both schedules reproduce the displayed assignment. Their likelihoods over repeated assignments differ, and randomization supplies an inferential basis, but the one realization does not reveal each missing potential outcome. Likewise, the fitted λvalues do not uniquely identify a structural funding channel; a different demand schedule or interaction can generate the same observed components. Treat Note B as a conditional mechanism model and test its restrictions in new evidence rather than label a fit proof of mechanism.

4. A complete prospective proposal

Title and question: “Additional borrower credit after funding offers: a linked-cohort study.” The question is whether offers expand total financing to fixed pre-offer borrowers, and how much origin-bank expansion is offset elsewhere. The primary estimand is the equal-borrower mean effect of assignment on total credit at ninety days in a newly defined eligible population. The target population, borrower weights and cohort overlaps must be settled before assignment. This is a proposal, not an approved or conducted study.

Mechanism and alternatives: lower funding cost may expand origin-bank credit; borrowers may substitute away from other lenders. Demand differences, eligibility selection, credit reclassification and competition spillovers are alternative explanations for an observational contrast. A valid offer lottery addresses assignment selection but does not by itself isolate the funding-cost channel or remove interference. Collect pre-offer funding exposure and comparable loan terms to formulate channel predictions; label channel analyses exploratory unless separately designed and justified.

Design and measurement: negotiate access to origin-bank and across-lender borrower records with the actual data owners and review authority. Construct a fixed eligible roster, audited identifiers and a cross-lender coverage report before assignment. If spillovers can be contained within markets, randomize sufficiently many eligible markets in prespecified matched pairs and aggregate borrower outcomes at that assignment level; if that containment is implausible, stop this design and redesign saturation/spillover measurement. Do not apply the six-bank toy randomization as though it solved a different cluster design. Freeze units, assignment probabilities, exclusions, baseline/date1windows and weighting; retain offered non-takers in the assignment-effect analysis.

Primary analysis and uncertainty: one confirmatory outcome is total ninety-day credit to the fixed eligible borrower population. Own-bank and other-lender components are accounting secondary outcomes, not three independent confirmatory wins. Prespecify the pair-weighted assignment estimator, exact randomization mechanism and a valid uncertainty procedure for the chosen assignment units. A sharp-null test answers its own null; confidence statements for the average effect require an appropriate justified procedure. Use blinded historical variance/cluster information and a substantively chosen minimum effect to compute prospective power and feasible assignment counts before launch; record assumptions, take-up and attrition scenarios. The current three-pair two-sided test cannot reject at5%, so it is not an adequate confirmatory template. Do not invent a sample-size calculation without those missing inputs.

Integrity, access and contingencies: document permissions, purpose limits, data minimization, secure access and authorized release conditions before obtaining real identifiable records. Hash and retain each authorized raw vintage; create a de-identified linkage layer only under the approved plan. Independent reconciliation of aggregate balances and source-specific units precedes outcome unblinding. If a source restates an entry, preserve the old result, record the correction and propagate all outputs. If total-credit coverage is incomplete, stop the original complete-data claim and report a defended missing-component bound or a separately approved narrower target. Do not silently use origin-bank lending as total credit. Safety or operational suspension is governed by actual oversight, not a fictional permission in this proposal.

Deliverables and feasibility decision: before launch, produce a target/assignment contract, access decision, coverage audit, power analysis and timestamped analysis plan with known information recorded. Registration requires an actual registry submission if used; this paragraph is not one. After analysis, release authorized code, documentation, synthetic test data and results with disclosure review; restricted records remain in their approved environment. Stop if access cannot support linked total credit, interference invalidates the unit, the powered design is unaffordable, or oversight declines the plan. A narrowed descriptive paper is an honest fallback but must be labeled and evaluated as such.

5. Sensitivity results and a complete short paper

Let ηbe the assignment contrast in credit omitted from the observed total, in millions per cohort. If η∈[−3,1], adding it to2gives (-1,3). These bounds are sharp for the measurement contrast: choose the omitted component's difference at either endpoint or any intermediate value, without altering the observed ledger. Nonnegative component levels can realize any such finite contrast by adding a sufficiently large common baseline. This is not a confidence interval or an identified causal-effect set; it is a range for the corrected observed contrast under a stated measurement scenario. Its credibility requires external coverage evidence.

At transported λ=5/4and main-policy choices(8,12,16), other-lender changes become(−10,−15,−20)and borrower changes(−2,−3,−4). Their mean is -3. Other-lender stocks(10,15,20)remain nonnegative. Own-bank lending is still positive, but net borrower credit falls because response stability failed. This is a constructed counterexample, not a forecast of actual crowding out.

Funding support, borrower substitution and a consequential ledger correction

Abstract. This synthetic research note reconstructs an apparent6million borrower-credit contrast from a paired-offer ledger and documents a restatement that reduces it to2million per cohort. Origin-bank lending remains12million above the paired comparison, with an offsetting−10million other-lender contrast. Under a stipulated three-pair lottery and no interference, the exact two-sided sharp-null p-value is1/4. A constrained funding-cost model can reproduce the component pattern, but its parameters are assumed and its national response is not identified. The exercise shows why version control, outcome scope and inferential limits belong in the main claim.

1. Question and contribution. Lending at a supported bank is not the same outcome as total credit available to its original borrowers. A borrower can shift lenders, and an erroneous component balance can change the apparent net expansion. This note's contribution is an explicit instructional reconstruction connecting those two issues. It claims neither new empirical evidence nor a gap established in the banking literature. The bounded related-method map above explains why linked borrower data and lender-side exposure matter; further substantive literature review is required before an original research claim.

2. Data and methods. The six synthetic cohorts contain100borrowers each and are fixed before a pairwise offer lottery. Each cohort's date0and date1credit is the sum of origin-bank and other-lender stocks, converted from raw thousands to millions. Version0has24cells; version1restates only CA's other-lender date1balance from26to14million. We retain both released calculations. The estimator averages offered-minus-control changes in the three pairs. Under the stated lottery and no interference it is design-unbiased for the equal-cohort assignment effect. Exact sharp-null inference enumerates the eight assignment patterns; it does not impute outcomes under a weak mean-zero null.

3. Results and mechanism. The restatement reduces the total contrast by4million because one of three offered-minus-control comparisons falls12. The unchanged p-value reflects the same relative extremeness in an eight-assignment reference list; it does not make the changed effect magnitude irrelevant. The component identity shows a much larger origin-bank contrast than net borrower contrast. An assumed model with concave lending payoffs and displacement can generate this pattern at subsidy4. Its unique constrained choices are8,12,16and implied net gains2each, with subsidy spending144under a150budget. Matching these numbers does not identify the channel or establish welfare. At subsidy8capacity binds, spending336is infeasible under that budget, and proportional scaling fails.

4. Robustness and limits. The stipulated lottery, complete across-lender coverage and lack of cross-cohort spillovers are maintained conditions. The sample is tiny: both exact sharp-null p-values are1/4, and nonrejection is not evidence of no effect. If omitted credit contributes an unknown contrast in[−3,1], the measured-plus-omitted contrast spans[−1,3]. If a new environment changes displacement to5/4, the model's main-policy mean borrower response becomes−3despite positive bank expansion. These are sensitivity assumptions, not probabilities or externally verified bounds. No national target weights, equilibrium competition model or welfare criterion are available.

5. Conclusion and reproducibility. The defensible numerical result is the corrected2million paired borrower-credit contrast alongside12and−10component contrasts, with explicit assignment uncertainty. The stronger original policy statement is withdrawn. The accompanying five-file release reproduces both vintages, their correction, exact assignment lists and conditional model diagnostics. It contains only original synthetic inputs. A real contribution requires newly justified evidence, an access-compliant design, a substantive literature comparison and independent expert review; the present demonstration supplies a rehearsal for that work.

Appendix. The optimizer projection proof and paired-estimator expectation appear in the instructor model artifact; the complete version comparison and raw ledger are above and downloadable. All reported values use exact rational arithmetic. No restricted data, empirical result from a cited paper or human assessment record was reproduced.

6. Completed release and ethics audit

The reader API run(data)returns strict JSON without printing, writing or changing its input. The default CLI quietly writes the neighboring output; explicit input/output paths are supported. Before any write, the CLI rejects direct, resolved, symbolic-link and existing-hardlink aliases of input, code, README and manifest. A learner audit must actually attempt those writes in disposable copies and verify all protected bytes remain unchanged, rather than merely call a guard helper. Never test destructive aliases on the only copy of research evidence.

The independent verification constructs all selected cells and pair estimates from raw primitives, enumerates sign assignments separately and optimizes the concave objective by comparing feasible candidates. It then compares the full reader result, not just a headline. Malformed domains, duplicate/unmatched/missing cells, invalid assignment and nonpositive model curvature are rejected. In contrast, subsidy4with budget100is a valid economic input: the result carries the spending144budget-failure diagnostic. It is not a parsing error and is never represented as feasible.

For a real continuation, inventory every source owner, authorized purpose, linkage permission, retention rule, privacy risk and release decision with the actual responsible authority. Minimize identifiers, separate linkage keys from analysis fields, review small-cell and linkage disclosure risks, and release only permitted artifacts. If raw data cannot be public, provide authorized access instructions and synthetic tests without implying public synthetic data independently verify the confidential estimates. Consent, de-identification or public availability alone must not be asserted as universal permission. The matrix here completes a synthetic release audit; it grants no authority for future real records.

7. Full defense responses and the real-research bridge

Examiner: Why did6become2? “One offered cohort's other-lender balance was restated downward by12million. That lowers one pair contrast by12and the average of three by4. Own-bank outcomes did not change. I preserve6as the reproduction of version0and use2as the corrected version1result; I do not describe the revision as new independent evidence.”

Examiner: The p-value stayed1/4. Was the correction immaterial? “No. The statistic's reference distribution changed with the data, and the observed value remained one of the two most extreme assignments out of eight. The resulting tail fraction happens to match. The estimated magnitude and other-lender component changed materially. Unchanged significance language cannot substitute for auditing the effect size.”

Examiner: Does subsidy8double the response? “No. The unconstrained solution would double, but all three capacities bind at subsidy8. Choices become10,14,18; the mean bank increment is14and mean borrower increment85/36, rather than24and4. Spending is336, above150. I must withdraw the global interior theorem and the proportional scale claim.”

Examiner: What if displacement is5/4and the budget100? “At the main subsidy the conditional borrower responses become−2,−3,−4, mean−3, while spending remains144and fails the100budget. There are two distinct failures: an adverse net-credit response under changed structural assumptions and insufficient financing. Neither is fixed by the positive origin-bank response. No welfare criterion or actual policy authority has been supplied.”

Examiner: What would make this original research? “The synthetic calculation alone cannot. I need a precise contribution relative to the closest actual papers, evidence or a new justified theoretical result that addresses that gap, an access-compliant reproducible analysis, and independent expert assessment of the resulting paper. Changing parameters or polishing this instructor paper is not enough. An inconclusive or negative finding can be defensible research if its design and contribution are substantive.”

Observation record template: record reviewer expertise/conflicts, artifact hashes and version, date, actual question, unedited answer, prompts given, independent versus prompted reasoning, material error, requested repair and reassessment result. Required domains are claim/contribution, measurement/reproducibility/ethics, model/design, uncertainty/writing and defense/revision. Blank fields mean “not observed,” not “passed.” An instructor's scripted answers cannot fill the learner's record. The later cross-volume research-portfolio package supplies a distinct capstone submission and defense protocol; this rehearsal and continuation plan do not represent that package or the learner's original contribution as complete.

Each criterion is scored once under its displayed domain. For a criterion worth n, award up to nfor the actual supplied reasoning/artifact, deducting for each substantive omitted or incorrect required element; document deductions and do not use prose length as a proxy. Full credit on reports/proposal/paper requires complete written artifacts, not promises or a checklist. Alternative defensible design choices can earn full credit when assumptions, feasibility and target changes are explicit. Invented research novelty or human approval, an unsupported causal/welfare conclusion, silent version mixing, missing-as-zero, or an infeasible policy treated as executable is a critical error requiring correction regardless of total.

Oral transfer: answer an unfamiliar challenge

After the written form, use a proposed 30-minute session with a human evaluator. The five prompts below are practice specimens, 4 points each. For a recorded advancement attempt, the evaluator must change the case or assumption before the learner sees it, retain the exact new prompt and independently verify its answer. Use one follow-up to test a weak assumption. Record whether each point was demonstrated independently, only after a cue, or not demonstrated; a cue-dependent point does not count as independent success. Require at least 17/20, at least 3/4 per task and correction of every critical error. These are proposed instructional criteria. A script read aloud is practice, not evidence of spontaneous defense.

  1. Two papers, one evidential base. An unfamiliar panel member says: “Two studies confirm the mechanism.” You are given only these descriptions: Note P regresses bank stock changes on funding access in ledger L; Note Q uses the same banks, dates and ledger L but divides changes by opening stocks. Both are observational, and their full methods have not been supplied. Give a bounded oral response, a useful next question and a decision about whether the evidence establishes independent replication.
  2. Carry a correction through the argument. During a defense, a verified correction changes one bank’s closing stock; (opening, original closing, corrected closing) are (80,96,88). The original abstract claimed “20% growth proves improved credit access.” The program faithfully reproduced 96. Calculate the corrected growth and its change in percentage points, then give an immediate response and release plan.
  3. Respond to selective significance. A study predeclared two outcomes as one family and a Bonferroni familywise level and valid unadjusted p-values (0.05,0.03,0.04). A discussant calls both confirmatory discoveries because each is below 0.05. Correct the decision and explain what the p-values do not establish about power or identification. Assume the stated p-values are valid under their respective nulls.
  4. Transport a result under challenge. There are two observed types. Source type shares are (1/2,1/2) and causal effects are (1,3). Target shares are (3/4,1/4). Compute source and transported effects if type-specific effects are stable. Then allow target effects (-1,1), with the same support and shares. Give the actual target effect and an oral response to “overlap guarantees transport.”
  5. Defend an incomplete portfolio honestly. A candidate has a runnable code archive and a friendly practice talk. The literature review includes only abstracts; the paper’s central proposition has no checked proof; no qualified external reader has evaluated novelty. The candidate asks the panel to certify an independent original contribution. Give a complete decision, a prioritized revision request and a defensible continuation gate.
Complete answers and additive scoring

  1. A complete response is: “These are two analyses of one underlying set of observations. The denominator change may answer a useful different measurement question, but it does not create independent data. Neither description states an assignment mechanism or sufficient adjustment conditions, so I cannot yet infer causality. I would obtain both full methods and exact sample/variable definitions, trace their common ledger and compare estimands and identifying restrictions. A feasible question is whether the funding-access association survives a predeclared measurement correction within the common sample. I cannot yet claim an original mechanism result or independent replication.” Even matching signs may result from shared data errors. A changed formula can be an extension of an analysis while leaving the evidence dependent.

    Rubric (4 points). Shared evidence 1; causal/source limits 1; concrete next question and inspection 1; bounded contribution/replication decision 1.

  2. Original growth is 16/80=1/5; corrected growth is 8/80=1/10, a change of −10 percentage points: (1/5,1/10,-10). A response is: “The correction halves the measured growth to 10%. Our program reproduced the old source but could not validate its value. I withdraw the 20% claim and the causal access language: a bank stock increase by itself does not establish improved access. I will preserve the original release, document the verified source correction, rerun affected tables and figures, revise the abstract and conclusion, and label the corrected version clearly.” Check other records derived from the same source and whether sample membership or weights change. Do not silently overwrite the input or claim that agreement with old output refutes the correction.

    Rubric (4 points). Rates/change 1; bounded immediate statement 1; complete propagation/version plan 1; reproduction and source-validity distinction 1.

  3. Each comparison uses 0.05/2=0.025; neither rejects. The adjusted p-values are min(1,2p), giving (0.025,0.06,0.08). Under either or both true nulls, the probability of at least one false rejection is at most the sum of the two valid marginal bounds, at most 0.05; independence is unnecessary. A suitable response is: “Both point estimates may be interesting, but neither clears the declared confirmatory rule. Report all outcomes, their intervals and the family definition; label further exploration. These realized p-values do not tell us the design’s prospective power, and valid testing of a statistical contrast does not supply its missing causal identification.” Do not retroactively split the family to rescue a result.

    Rubric (4 points). Threshold and decisions 1; adjusted values 1; union-bound logic 1; prospective power/causality and honest reporting 1.

  4. The source mean is 2; stable-effect transport yields (3/4)1+(1/4)3=3/2. With changed target effects it is (3/4)(−1)+(1/4)1=−1/2. Thus (2,3/2,-1/2). A response is: “Overlap means both target types occur in the source. It allows the weighting operation but does not ensure that interventions, mechanisms, implementation or effect modifiers are comparable. The same overlap is consistent with a target effect of −1/2. I need a justified conditional effect-stability argument, correct type measurement and target shares, and a common intervention/outcome definition; otherwise I would present the 3/2 estimate as conditional and analyze departures.” This counterexample changes conditional effects, not merely population composition.

    Rubric (4 points). Source/conditional transport 1; counterexample value 1; overlap versus stability 1; concrete conditions and qualified response 1.

  5. A defensible decision is: “The archive and talk are useful evidence of preparation, but originality and correctness remain unestablished. I would not certify the contribution yet. First state the exact proposition, domain and assumptions, finish its proof or revise it around a counterexample, and reconcile the paper’s claims with that result. Read the closest full papers and build a claim-by-claim comparison. Then submit a versioned paper, source map, proof and reproduction materials to qualified readers who can challenge both novelty and validity. Keep their actual comments and a response memo, and conduct a defense with unseen changes of assumption. Continue only when material objections are answered or the contribution is narrowed honestly.” A favorable private conversation is not a documented evaluation of the unresolved tasks. Passing the synthetic exercise records rehearsal success only.

    Rubric (4 points). Evidence-based decision 1; prioritized correctness and literature work 1; exact external submission/response 1; honest continuation/defense gate 1.

Delayed retention and changed transfer

After a proposed three-week interval, attempt these five new tasks in 90 minutes without notes or code, using a basic calculator. Each carries 8 points. Require at least 34/40, at least 6/8 per task and correction of critical errors. If the learner has already studied these answers, administer materially changed cases with independently checked solutions. Preserve the delay, exact task, first attempt, assistance and correction rather than representing familiarity as retention. Thresholds and timing are not calibrated.

  1. Reconstruct a literature decision. After a study interval, use only these complete fictional notes. Note U: “For four banks with opening stocks 10 each and closing stocks (11,11,9,9), mean individual growth is zero. We describe one period without treatment variation; the observation cannot estimate a funding-policy effect.” Note V: “Using the same records as U, total opening and closing stocks are both 40. Aggregate growth is zero. This confirms a new causal law: funding policy never changes lending.” Write a small evidence map and a concise referee reply to V, including a feasible follow-up question. Do not invent other literature or an actual policy assignment.
  2. Rebuild an aggregate from units. Bank A reports opening and closing stocks (1.2,1.3) million. Bank B reports (400,440) thousand of the same currency. Construct common-unit totals, aggregate growth and equal-bank mean growth. State a unit test and write a two-sentence results note including what is not identified.
  3. Repair a design before observing outcomes. For a prospective equal-arm independent-sample normal-mean comparison, use the supplied approximate planning formula n≈2σ²(zα/2+zpower)²/δ² per arm. Assume (common known σ, target difference δ, zα/2, zpower)=(2,1,1.96,0.84), for two-sided 5% significance and target power 80%. Compute the integer per-arm and total target. Capacity is only 120 completed observations. State a feasible prospective response and two reasons this calculation may not describe an actual field design.
  4. Report bias separately from sampling error. A normal benchmark estimate of an effect and its known standard error are (0.9,0.2). Suppose the estimator’s mean is θ+b, where unknown bias b lies in [0,B]. Use the supplied rounded 1.96 quantile. Derive an interval that covers θ whenever the usual sampling-error event holds. Compute it for B=0.4 and B=0.6; explain whether a positive effect is robust in each case and whether the bias limit was estimated.
  5. Choose the next research step. A paper’s code reproduces its tables. Its theoretical counterexample is correct on a documented parameter domain. Two closest papers have now been read fully, but no new data have been collected. A qualified reader writes: “The counterexample may be useful; I cannot yet tell whether the claimed mechanism is distinct from the second paper.” A separate reviewer identifies a restricted dataset whose access has not been granted. Write a response memo, a next-month research plan with exact hours totaling at most 80, and a stop or revision rule. Do not claim that an encouraging comment establishes originality.
Complete answers and additive scoring

  1. The map has two rows: U uses four equally sized banks, estimates mean individual growth, reports zero and explicitly limits its conclusion to a descriptive period; V reuses exactly the same data, estimates aggregate stock growth, also obtains zero, and adds an unsupported causal law. Both share one evidence base. The individual rates are (1/10,1/10,−1/10,−1/10); both reported zeroes are correct because opening weights are equal. (0,0) checks the means. A full reply is: “Your aggregate accounting calculation is correct, but it neither provides independent evidence nor estimates a policy effect. With no assignment or counterfactual, many policy effects can coexist with zero observed aggregate growth. Replace the causal-law claim with the descriptive reconciliation, explain why the two estimands agree here, and retain the shared-data provenance. A useful follow-up is whether changed opening weights make bank-average and aggregate growth diverge in a documented panel. A causal extension requires a separately defended design and actual evidence.” This comparison supports a limited measurement contribution in the supplied dossier; a broader novelty claim requires reading and searching the real literature.

    Rubric (8 points). Two accurate map rows 2; arithmetic and equal-weight explanation 2; major concern with counterfactual reasoning 2; constructive repair and bounded follow-up 2.

  2. Express B as (0.4,0.44) million. Total stocks are 1.6 and 1.74 million; growth is 0.14/1.6=7/80. Individual rates are 1/12 and 1/10, whose equal mean is 11/120. The checked tuple is (1.6,1.74,7/80,11/120). Opening-stock weights (3/4,1/4) applied to individual rates recover 7/80. A unit test converts both records instead to thousands and verifies unchanged growth and totals multiplied by 1000; rejecting missing or contradictory unit labels prevents silent addition of incompatible scales. A results note is: “Outstanding stock for the two recorded banks rose from 1.6 to 1.74 million, or 8.75%; equal-bank growth was approximately 9.17%. These descriptive stock measures do not establish new originations, a causal intervention effect or growth outside the two-bank population.” Preserve the raw unit labels and transformation log.

    Rubric (8 points). Normalization/totals 2; two growth estimands and weights 2; meaningful unit test/provenance 2; bounded two-sentence writing 2.

  3. The continuous target is 2×4×(2.8)²=62.72, so round up to 63 per arm, 126 total. Capacity is short by 6: (62.72,63,126,6). The formula is a planning approximation, not an exact guarantee even in its benchmark model. One defensible response is to seek capacity for six more completed observations before launch; if unavailable, retain balanced 60-person arms and explicitly revise the feasibility/power claim, or narrow the proposed question using a separately justified effect target and replan before looking at outcomes. Do not silently describe 120 as the originally calculated target or change the primary outcome after inspecting significance. Clustered assignment changes effective information; differential attrition can lower sample size and threaten identification; noncompliance changes the estimand or detectable contrast. Document assignment, outcome timing, exclusions, familywise rule and contingencies prospectively. A larger sample cannot repair an invalid comparison.

    Rubric (8 points). Formula substitution 2; rounding/total/capacity 2; honest prospective repair 2; two concrete design limitations with identification distinction 2.

  4. On the event |estimate−(θ+b)|≤1.96×0.2=0.392, θ lies in [estimate−b−0.392, estimate−b+0.392]. Taking the union over b∈[0,B] gives [0.508−B,1.292]. For B=0.4 it is [0.108,1.292]; for B=0.6 it is [−0.092,1.292]. Thus (0.108,1.292,-0.092,1.292). The first excludes zero positively under its maintained bias bound and normal sampling model; the second includes zero and negative values. The bias-adjusted point-effect sets [0.5,0.9] and [0.3,0.9] are both positive, but they omit sampling uncertainty. Neither B value was learned from these three numerical inputs: each is a substantive sensitivity restriction requiring justification. The union argument ensures at least the sampling event’s approximate 95% coverage for any fixed permitted b; it does not assign probabilities to bias values or claim exact 95% coverage of the wider union.

    Rubric (8 points). Sampling event and union derivation 2; both intervals 2; point versus interval/sign distinctions 2; assumption and coverage scope 2.

  5. A complete response memo is: “Thank you for separating the valid counterexample from its contribution. I will add a side-by-side comparison with the second paper, including its maintained assumptions, mechanism and claimed domain. I will ask you to review the precise distinction and revise or withdraw the novelty statement if the example is already implied there. The unapproved dataset will not enter the analysis; I will investigate authorized access and document feasibility without claiming results. The current paper remains a theory-based candidate contribution with reproducible illustrative tables.” A feasible 80-hour plan assigns 25 to the mechanism/assumption comparison, 20 to proof and boundary extensions, 15 to the revised paper and response, 10 to qualified feedback and preparation for unseen defense, and 10 to access feasibility or a public-data alternative. (25,20,15,10,10,80) records the allocation. End the month with a versioned revised proposition, comparison and response, not a promised acceptance. If the closest paper subsumes the result, narrow to a clearly labeled pedagogical counterexample or replace the research question; if access is denied, drop or redesign the empirical extension. Do not interpret a delayed response as approval. Preserve actual feedback and acknowledge which gates remain incomplete.

    Rubric (8 points). Specific response and contribution comparison 2; honest access/evidence status 2; feasible exact plan/deliverables 2; substantive stop/revision and external-review gate 2.

Remediation and coverage map

The written forms and seven-task project cover all twelve chapters at the bounded depth specified in their rubrics. The support tasks sample prerequisites and transfer; they are not a substitute for each chapter’s exercises. Diagnose the reasoning failure, revisit the indicated chapter and solve a genuinely changed task before reassessment. D, O and R denote diagnostic, oral and retention tasks. A/B denote the two written forms and their five domains.

Notation and interpretation

Symbols and terms with their conditions
ChapterNotation or termMeaning and scope
01Research question and contributionA claim about a defined population, mechanism or theorem; feasibility and originality are separate judgments.
02Evidence mapA source-by-claim record of data, method, estimand, result and limits; source dependence matters.
03Version; reproductionA specified set of inputs/code/results; reproduction here uses the same input evidence and stated computation, without proving validity.
04Major concern; referee recommendationA consequential issue for the central claim and an evidence-based evaluation; recommendation is not a fact about acceptance.
05τ, b and DOutcome units: causal effect, differential untreated change and observed change contrast; in D2, D=τ+b.
06q, p and S(q)Quantity, currency per quantity and total surplus; domain q≥0 and quasilinear/no-externality conditions matter.
07μmiss; observation unitMean of missing outcomes in outcome units; bank, borrower and event records are different units and cannot be silently interchanged.
08α, power, n and δType-I error probability, rejection probability at a stipulated alternative, observations per arm and target difference in outcome units; all design-dependent.
09B; target sharesNonnegative bias limit in outcome units, distinct from a standard error; type shares sum to one but do not ensure effect stability.
10Estimand; interval; percentage pointThe defined target quantity; a procedure with specified coverage assumptions; difference between percentages, distinct from percent change.
11Response memo; unseen transferA traceable objection-to-revision record; a new change of assumptions answered independently, not recitation.
12Portfolio gate; qualified evaluationAn actual evidence requirement that cannot be offset by unrelated points; a real reviewer’s substantive judgment, not an invented or anticipated approval.

Concept index

Use the chapter-linked remediation table as the chapter index: agenda and feasibility (1); source dependence and critical reading (2); versions and computational reproduction (3); constructive referee reports (4); counterfactual identification (5); theory and boundary discipline (6); data measurement and ethics (7); prospective power and analysis rules (8); sensitivity and transport (9); evidence-aligned writing (10); defense and revision (11); actual contribution and external evaluation (12). No single score removes the need to inspect these distinct capabilities.

From research rehearsal to real scholarship

The central chain is question → evidence and assumptions → argument → challenge → revision. A failure at one link changes what the whole paper can claim. A correct proof need not be novel; a reproducible table need not measure the intended object; a credible source-population effect need not transport; and a clear talk need not withstand an unfamiliar objection. Preserve these distinctions in the final paper and portfolio rather than hiding them in appendices.

To continue, choose a narrow question, read the closest full research, establish feasible and warranted access, complete the appropriate proof or empirical design, and maintain a reproducible claim-to-output record. Submit actual work to qualified readers, respond to consequential objections, and defend a changed assumption. The later research capstone organizes this submission and examination; the teaching volume then asks you to teach these reasoning processes and evaluate another learner’s work. Leadership later adds responsibility for people and resources. The library supplies instruction and protocols; those human achievements remain to be demonstrated.

Source scope and original material

All case records, numerical tasks, answers, scoring and proposed timing here are original instructional material. Methods are taught in the linked accepted chapters. Terminology follows the bounded distinction in the National Academies’ 2019 summary on reproducibility and replicability: a successful same-data computation does not by itself establish correctness or an independent new-data result. The AEA Data and Code Availability Policy, inspected February 2026 version is a professional benchmark for documenting data/code provenance, output reproduction and restricted-access limitations; it is not a claim that this exercise satisfies a journal’s requirements or grants data permission. Retained source inspection scopes and reviewer roles are recorded separately. Internal author/agent checking is not independent human academic certification. Rendered browser, mobile, keyboard and print review remain subject to the recorded access limitation.
